meta.title: MMURM Foundation — independent re-performance of the Julius AI test suite
meta.source_document: MMURM_LHC_Foundation (Anthony Castro / Julius AI session analyses, data circa Sep 2025)
meta.spec: tests/TEST_CENSUS.md (38 tracked items: 30 tests + 8 registered claims; plus 2026-10-23 addenda: Groups X and I, 4 items each, and registry claims URM-9/URM-10; plus 2026-10-24 addendum: Group M, 5 items, and registry claim URM-11)

honesty_labels.REPRODUCTION: recomputed from inputs fully specified in the document
honesty_labels.RECONSTRUCTION: document publishes summaries, not raw data; dataset regenerated from the published summaries under a fixed seed
honesty_labels.PROTOCOL: requires experimental facilities; registered, not re-run
honesty_labels.DERIVATION-CHECK: a claimed derivation is re-performed from the parameters the source itself states; unstated inputs are swept, never assumed
honesty_labels.REPORTED-ONLY: values recorded as reported; the underlying computation was not supplied, so nothing is presented as verified

provenance_notes: The source document's 'weighted confidence' scores (84.6%, updated 89.3%) are a self-assigned scoring rubric, not a statistical test. They are recorded here for provenance and are NOT re-issued as findings.
The document gives lambda_1 as both 3.70 and 2.80 in different sections; this suite reports the value recomputed from the published correlation matrix (see S1).

Addenda (2026-10-23, author-supplied, NOT part of the original 38): Group X audits the 800-1600-year Lindblad half-decoherence claim from the author's decoherence memo against the manuscript's stated parameters; Group I audits the inverse structural solver's N=5 result. Claims URM-9 and URM-10 register both in the registry.

S_statistics.test: Eigenvalue spectrum of the 5x5 correlation matrix
S_statistics.label: REPRODUCTION (published matrix is fully specified)
flags: TRACE VIOLATION: the published eigenvalues (3.70, 0.80, 0.50, 0.30, 0.10) sum to 5.40, but every 5x5 correlation matrix has trace exactly 5, so its eigenvalues must sum to 5. The published spectrum is not the spectrum of the published matrix, nor of any 5x5 correlation matrix.

The document also prints lambda_1 = 2.80 in its cascade section ('2.80 (report) or 3.70 (plot)') while using 3.70 elsewhere; the recomputed value from its own matrix is 3.635 — neither printed number.

The Marchenko-Pastur edge for the actual case (p=5, n=22) is 2.18, not the printed 1.97 (and not the plot's 1.0 line). lambda_1 does exceed the correct edge, so the qualitative 'one dominant mode' reading survives; the printed numbers do not.
S_statistics.notes: Eigenvalues recomputed from data/ensemble22_correlation_published.csv. The published matrix itself is a valid correlation matrix (min eigenvalue > 0).

S_statistics.label: RECONSTRUCTION

published_result.basis_as_printed: covariance ('PCA is on covariance, not correlation')

flags: In natural units the covariance PCA is dominated by t_half (values 800-1600 yr; variance orders of magnitude larger than the other observables), giving PC1 ~= 100% — the published 0.30/0.24/0.19/0.16/0.11 profile cannot arise from the documented distributions in natural units.

The correlation PCA gives yet another profile (~eigenvalues/5 of the sample correlation matrix). Neither recomputation matches the published ratios; the source simulation's variable scaling is undocumented, so the published PCA cannot be reproduced or audited (CANNOT AGREE on method, DIFFERS on numbers).
S_statistics.notes: The document's own resolution ('after standardization -> correlation PCA -> PC1 dominates') contradicts its printed covariance ratios, which show PC1 at only 30%.

S_statistics.test: Bootstrap correlation sin^2(theta_W) vs M_Amat, 800 resamples
S_statistics.label: RECONSTRUCTION

published_result.claimed: p < 0.001, 'highly significant due to large n=22 realities'

flags: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the document's bootstrap centres on r ~= 0.10 for sin^2(theta_W) vs M_Amat, but its own published correlation matrix gives r = 0.926 for the same pair. A bootstrap of data with correlation 0.926 cannot centre on 0.10. The reconstruction (built on the published matrix) bootstraps around r ~= 0.89. One of the two published artefacts does not describe the ensemble.

SIGNIFICANCE ERROR: at n = 22, r = 0.10 gives t = 0.45, p = 0.66 — nowhere near significant. 800 bootstrap resamples of 22 points do not create significance the sample does not contain; 'large n' is the resample count, not the sample size.
S_statistics.notes: Resampling 22 fixed points measures the stability of the estimate for THIS ensemble; it is not independent evidence about physics.

S_statistics.label: RECONSTRUCTION
S_statistics.verdict_scope: The published matrix is internally valid (symmetric, unit diagonal, positive definite) and is used verbatim as the reconstruction target. The n=22 reconstruction's sample correlations deviate by up to 0.34, which is ordinary sampling noise at n=22 — the matrix is a summary the document asserts, not a result this suite can confirm.
S_statistics.notes: Strong positive block sin2/DM/M_Amat (r = 0.80-0.93) and negative t_half couplings (r ~= -0.62..-0.70) are properties asserted by the document; no independent dataset exists to check them against.

S_statistics.test: Partial correlation sin^2(theta_W) <-> DM_sigma controlling M_Amat
S_statistics.label: REPRODUCTION (from published matrix) + RECONSTRUCTION (from data)
S_statistics.notes: The one ensemble statistic that reproduces cleanly: (0.898 - 0.926*0.800) / sqrt((1-0.926^2)(1-0.800^2)) = 0.694 vs published 0.692 (rounding). Agreement is with the document's own matrix arithmetic; it does not validate the matrix itself.

S_statistics.label: RECONSTRUCTION

flags: SELF-REFERENTIAL NULL: 140 GeV is URM's own predicted/median value, not an independent measurement (M_Amat is 'not in SM'). Deviations from it measure ensemble spread, not agreement with experiment.
An upper limit is used as a point null: every model value above the limit is a >= +50% 'deviation', so band membership tests the limit's misuse, not the model.
Model values are 800-1600 yr, ~7 orders of magnitude below this null; deviations are ~-100% by construction.
H_0 is NOT one of the 5 ensemble observables and has no published per-reality distribution; the document's H_0 band entries cannot be reconstructed or checked.

ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE AS PUBLISHED: the document's own ranges cap sin^2(theta_W) deviations at 2.8% (values 0.231-0.238 vs null 0.2315) and M_Amat at 2.9% (136-144 vs null 140) — both below the 5% band floor. No dataset consistent with the published distributions can put either observable in the 5-7.5% band, yet the document reports 6/6 co-occurrence for both.
DM_sigma: the published distribution (peaks 1.5/2.5/3.0) vs the LUX-ZEPLIN upper-limit 'null' of 1.0 gives deviations of +50% to +200% — above the band, not in it.
t_half 0/6 'agrees' only trivially: model values sit ~7 orders of magnitude below the >1e10 yr null (deviation ~-100%), not just outside a 5-7.5% band as a 'threshold effect'.
H_0 cannot be checked at all: it is not in the ensemble and has no published per-reality values.
S_statistics.notes: Run on the RECONSTRUCTION, but the caps above are pure arithmetic on the document's published ranges and nulls — they hold for ANY dataset matching those summaries, including the original one.

S_statistics.test: PC1 clustering of flagged realities + 10,000-resample bootstrap
S_statistics.label: RECONSTRUCTION

recomputed_result.status: NOT PERFORMABLE: under the published >=3-hit flag definition, zero realities are flagged in any dataset consistent with the published distributions and nulls (see S6), so there is no flagged group to cluster.

flags: The published p = 0.0008 clustering result presupposes 6 flagged realities whose band membership is arithmetically impossible under the document's own published ranges and nulls (S6). The clustering machinery is implemented here exactly as described (PC1 of the published correlation matrix; label-permutation bootstrap, 10,000 resamples) and runs the moment a dataset with flagged realities is supplied — on every dataset consistent with the published summaries, there is nothing to run it on.
S_statistics.notes: PC1 scores use the published matrix's dominant eigenvector applied to the standardised reconstruction.

X_decoherence.test: Memo's effective-rate conversion: t1/2 = 800-1600 yr corresponds to Gamma_eff = 4.33e-4 - 8.66e-4 /yr (1.37e-11 - 2.75e-11 /s)
X_decoherence.label: REPRODUCTION
X_decoherence.published_result: Gamma_eff = 4.33e-4 - 8.66e-4 yr^-1 = 1.37e-11 - 2.75e-11 s^-1; illustrative decomposition 7.5e-4 /yr -> t1/2 = 924 yr
X_decoherence.notes: The memo's arithmetic is correct. Correct unit conversion is not a derivation of the interval: the Gamma range is computed FROM 800-1600 yr, and the memo itself labels its component values illustrative.

X_decoherence.test: Lindblad computation from the manuscript's stated decoherence operator L = sqrt(gamma) sigma_z, gamma = 0.94 per recursion
X_decoherence.label: DERIVATION-CHECK
X_decoherence.published_result: Claim: the stated Lindblad framework yields t1/2 ~ 800-1600 yr
X_decoherence.verdict_scope: The stated operator yields t1/2 = 0.369 recursion steps. Reaching 800 yr requires a proper-time step of ~2,170 yr per recursion (~4,340 yr for 1600 yr); at any step duration the text suggests (phonon periods ~1e-14 s) the half-life is ~1e-22 yr.

X_decoherence.test: Modal dynamics: does any stated mode supply the slow decay? gamma_k = 0.94(1 - delta_k1), lambda_1 = 3.71, c_kj = eps*m_kj, eps = 0.15
X_decoherence.label: DERIVATION-CHECK
X_decoherence.published_result: Modal framework with 94% damping of non-core modes; core mode persistent
X_decoherence.verdict_scope: The stated modal drift is growth-dominated (max +3.10/step); the slowest decay anywhere is 0.024/step (t1/2 ~ 29 steps), and the core mode's intrinsic decay is exactly 0 by the delta_k1 factor. No stated mode decays anywhere near 1e-24/step.
flags: Prose/equation tension: the text calls gamma_k a 'damping factor', but the printed modal equation enters it as +gamma_k (lambda_1 - 1), a growth term for k > 1. The audit used the equation as printed.
omega_0 is stated as 1.0e14 rad/s in the constants table and 1.4e14 rad/s in the body text; immaterial at these orders of magnitude, recorded for the errata list.

X_decoherence.test: Protected-sector route: can Lindblad form (no signed budget) produce the interval, and at what price?
X_decoherence.label: DERIVATION-CHECK
X_decoherence.published_result: Memo's budget ansatz: Gamma_eff = Gamma_local + Gamma_leak + Gamma_branch - Gamma_recurrence - Gamma_topological

recomputed_result.mechanism: protected coherence decays at eps_leak/2, so t1/2 = 2 ln2 / eps_leak exactly (sweep-verified)

X_decoherence.verdict: CANNOT BE DERIVED from stated parameters — requirement identified
X_decoherence.verdict_scope: A protected sector with a leak channel yields arbitrarily long half-lives in strict Lindblad form (t1/2 = 2 ln2/eps_leak, sweep-verified), so the mechanism exists. But the 800-yr claim is then exactly equivalent to positing eps_leak ~ 1.2e-24 per step (at a G-band-period step) — a cancellation to ~3e-25 of the stated dephasing rate. No parameter stated in the manuscript fixes eps_leak or dtau at the required values. This does not disprove the interval; it converts it into one auditable assumption.

I_inverse_solver.test: Bridge relations imply B = (5N-4)/(N+2); positive-integer B over N=2..64 leaves only {5, 12}
I_inverse_solver.label: REPRODUCTION
I_inverse_solver.published_result: Admissible set {N=5 (B=3), N=12 (B=4)}; N=1 rejected (B not a positive integer)

recomputed_result.reason: B = 5 - 14/(N+2) is a positive integer only when (N+2) divides 14; in range only N+2 in {7, 14}

I_inverse_solver.test: Both candidate architectures satisfy the Euler closure chi = D - (T*B) + R; N=12 reproduces the legacy architecture (R=22, T=14, B=4, 56 channels, D=12, chi=-22)
I_inverse_solver.label: REPRODUCTION
I_inverse_solver.notes: The legacy architecture (22/14/4/12/-22), assembled before this solver, is one of only two integer solutions of the bridge system. The closure is a counting identity the architecture imposes on itself, not an independently computed Euler characteristic of a specified manifold.
flags: The bridge relations (g=N, D=N, T=N+2, R=-chi) carry all of the selective power and their provenance is not stated in the solver report: if they were abstracted from the legacy architecture, the N=12 reproduction is guaranteed by construction and N=5 is the other solution of a system built around the first; if derived independently, the {5, 12} admissible set is a discovery. The audit cannot distinguish these from the report alone.

I_inverse_solver.test: Topology free-energy sweep selects N=5 over N=12 (lower F wins)
I_inverse_solver.label: REPORTED-ONLY
I_inverse_solver.published_result: F(g=5) = -9.2023 vs F(g=12) = -0.6029; unrestricted sweep optimum is g=1, rejected on admissibility (see I1)
I_inverse_solver.recomputed_result: Not re-performed: the topology sweep itself (objective definition, code, data) was not supplied with the solver report, so the F values are recorded as reported, not verified.
flags: F has its unrestricted optimum at g=1, so the objective alone mostly prefers small genus; the admissibility filter performs the selection and F breaks a two-way tie. Depositing the sweep would upgrade this item to REPRODUCTION.

I_inverse_solver.test: Physical (Hawking) identification of the structural count N
I_inverse_solver.label: PROTOCOL
I_inverse_solver.published_result: Solver reports: Inference = provisional structural candidate (N=5); Physical Hawking identification = not yet established. The recovered Hawking temperature T_H = hbar*kappa/(2*pi*k_B*c) contains no structural N.
I_inverse_solver.recomputed_result: Agrees with the solver's own labeling: no H(N) — a Hawking-side observable depending on N — exists in the supplied material, so no independent test of N=5 against Hawking physics can be performed.
I_inverse_solver.notes: Stated next milestone (from the solver report): derive an independent H(N). If a Hawking-side quantity lands near N=5 without passing through the bridge relations, the candidate upgrades from internal structure to evidence.

A_architecture.test: Branch-dependent derived objects, recomputed per branch from the manuscript's stated formulas
A_architecture.label: DERIVATION-CHECK
A_architecture.published_result: Published objects exist for the N=12 branch only (manuscript passim; Groups S/E ensemble at n=22; lambda_1 = 3.71 of the 12-layer modal object)
A_architecture.verdict: COMPUTED for both branches — see notes
A_architecture.notes: P_shadow prefactor Gamma(R)/Gamma(D): N=5 -> 210; N=12 -> 21!/11!. Marchenko-Pastur edge (p=5): n=8 -> 3.21 vs n=22 -> 2.18 (the S1-corrected edge is the 12-branch value). The N=5 branch currently has NO ensemble statistics and NO lambda_1: at n=8 those must be newly simulated, and nothing in the 12-branch results transfers.

A_architecture.test: Identification of the Eq. 11.1 prefactor Gamma(5)/zeta(2) = 14.59 under parameterization
A_architecture.label: DERIVATION-CHECK
A_architecture.published_result: Phi_total (Eq. 11.1) carries prefactor Gamma(5)/zeta(2) = 14.59 in the legacy (N=12) text
flags: If the prefactor's argument is the structural N, the printed 14.59 is consistent ONLY with N=5 (at N=12 it would be ~2.43e7). If it is an independent constant, it is branch-invariant and the match at N=5 is coincidence. The supplied material does not decide between these readings; recorded as an open identification, not as evidence for either branch.

M_modal.test: N = 5 modal system: frequencies, damping, weight convention
M_modal.label: CONSTRUCTION
M_modal.published_result: Legacy (N = 12): 12 modes, omega_k = omega_0 / F_k, gamma_k = 0.94(1 - delta_k1), modal weights summing to 1 (printed 1.006), U_core = lam_1 = 3.71 [simulated]. No 5-branch modal specification exists in the supplied material.

recomputed_result.modal_matrix_definition: 5x5 correlation matrix of modal amplitudes across the 8 realities; eigenvalues lam_k, trace 5; modal weights w_k = lam_k / 5, sum 1
recomputed_result.convention_note: w_1 = lam_1 / 5 BY DEFINITION on this branch, so the legacy weight/variance conflation (manuscript R3) cannot recur

M_modal.notes: Mode identities: only mode 1 carries a branch-invariant meaning (core/fundamental resonance, by the gamma_1 = 0 rule). The 12 legacy layer names are NOT mapped onto 5 modes — no such rule is stated, and inventing one would be fabrication. omega_0's dual stated value (1.0 vs 1.4e14 rad/s, Group X flag) is why only ratios are used.

M_modal.label: CONSTRUCTION
M_modal.published_result: Legacy: (U_env)_ri = R_r . S_i, r, i = 1..22, Fibonacci diagonal dominance R_r . S_r proportional to F_r. No numerical entries are given even for the legacy matrix.

recomputed_result.diagonal_dominance: R_r . S_r proportional to F_r, F = (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21)

M_modal.notes: The 8x8 form is carried, not numerically instantiated: the reality amplitudes R_r and string modes S_i are never numerically specified in the supplied material. Any numeric U_env would be invention.

M_modal.label: SIMULATION
M_modal.published_result: No 5-branch ensemble exists (instantiation doc Section 4). Legacy: lam_1 = 3.71 +/- 0.04 at n = 1,000 realities; reconstruction 3.659 at n = 22 (E1).

M_modal.notes: Target correlation matrix reused as a STATED ASSUMPTION: it is the only published correlation structure, and nothing derives it for the 5-branch. t_half's marginal is carried as published; its null-status problem (Group S/E) is unchanged. The single dataset's lam1 is one draw of a wide distribution — see the p5/p95 spread.

M_modal.test: Modal-amplitude null ensemble: lam1_mod(5) under no coherence
M_modal.label: SIMULATION

M_modal.notes: Two bars, not one, and their order matters. S1: The document also prints lambda_1 = 2.80 in its cascade section ('2.80 (report) or 3.70 (plot)') while using 3.70 elsewhere; the recomputed value from its own matrix is 3.635 — neither printed number.

S1: The Marchenko-Pastur edge for the actual case (p=5, n=22) is 2.18, not the printed 1.97 (and not the plot's 1.0 line). lambda_1 does exceed the correct edge, so the qualitative 'one dominant mode' reading survives; the printed numbers do not.

S2: In natural units the covariance PCA is dominated by t_half (values 800-1600 yr; variance orders of magnitude larger than the other observables), giving PC1 ~= 100% — the published 0.30/0.24/0.19/0.16/0.11 profile cannot arise from the documented distributions in natural units.

S2: The correlation PCA gives yet another profile (~eigenvalues/5 of the sample correlation matrix). Neither recomputation matches the published ratios; the source simulation's variable scaling is undocumented, so the published PCA cannot be reproduced or audited (CANNOT AGREE on method, DIFFERS on numbers).

S3: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION: the document's bootstrap centres on r ~= 0.10 for sin^2(theta_W) vs M_Amat, but its own published correlation matrix gives r = 0.926 for the same pair. A bootstrap of data with correlation 0.926 cannot centre on 0.10. The reconstruction (built on the published matrix) bootstraps around r ~= 0.89. One of the two published artefacts does not describe the ensemble.

S3: SIGNIFICANCE ERROR: at n = 22, r = 0.10 gives t = 0.45, p = 0.66 — nowhere near significant. 800 bootstrap resamples of 22 points do not create significance the sample does not contain; 'large n' is the resample count, not the sample size.

S6: ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE AS PUBLISHED: the document's own ranges cap sin^2(theta_W) deviations at 2.8% (values 0.231-0.238 vs null 0.2315) and M_Amat at 2.9% (136-144 vs null 140) — both below the 5% band floor. No dataset consistent with the published distributions can put either observable in the 5-7.5% band, yet the document reports 6/6 co-occurrence for both.
S6: DM_sigma: the published distribution (peaks 1.5/2.5/3.0) vs the LUX-ZEPLIN upper-limit 'null' of 1.0 gives deviations of +50% to +200% — above the band, not in it.
S6: t_half 0/6 'agrees' only trivially: model values sit ~7 orders of magnitude below the >1e10 yr null (deviation ~-100%), not just outside a 5-7.5% band as a 'threshold effect'.
S6: H_0 cannot be checked at all: it is not in the ensemble and has no published per-reality values.

S7: The published p = 0.0008 clustering result presupposes 6 flagged realities whose band membership is arithmetically impossible under the document's own published ranges and nulls (S6). The clustering machinery is implemented here exactly as described (PC1 of the published correlation matrix; label-permutation bootstrap, 10,000 resamples) and runs the moment a dataset with flagged realities is supplied — on every dataset consistent with the published summaries, there is nothing to run it on.
